page_title: How our production team runs the weekly on-call handover

sources.entry: How our production team runs the weekly on-call handover

summary.name: GitLab on-call handover process
summary.one_liner: A 2018 GitLab blog post describing how its production team runs a weekly 30-minute on-call handover meeting and an automated "on-call robot assistant" that builds handover reports.
keywords: how to run on call handover
use_cases: Running a weekly on-call handover meeting
Structuring follow-the-sun on-call shifts across time zones
Reviewing seven-day performance metrics for anomalies
summary.what_it_does: The post explains that GitLab's production team assigns on-call shifts that follow the sun so engineers are not woken at night, and holds a 30-minute weekly on-call handover meeting. During the meeting the team reviews incidents from the last seven days, checks GitLab issues labelled on-call for items to carry into the next shift, and reviews seven-day graphs of key metrics. An in-house program called the on-call robot assistant pulls last-shift incidents from PagerDuty, generates issue stats from the production backlog, and renders seven-day Prometheus graphs into a GitLab issue. The current on-call engineer closes the report to end the shift.
notable: Follow-the-sun on-call shifts for a fully remote team across three time zones
On-call robot assistant generates handover reports as GitLab issues from PagerDuty, Grafana and Prometheus data
Handover reports are public in GitLab's issue tracker
caveats: Describes an internal 2018 process and tooling; the robot assistant is not presented as a released product
Occasional out-of-hours response is needed, with time off encouraged afterward
